investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint that backs POST /api/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer received a connection error when attempting to forward the agent-creation request to the swarm backend (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents), causing it to return HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway". This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. No evidence of a user-traffic or production-incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-detected availability gap.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 741 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval for check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 741 minutes old at eval time (2026-09-30T01:06:31Z), more than double the contract maximum of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the snapshot JSON, not to the website serving infrastructure itself.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot on disk is 741 minutes old, meaning the workflow either failed, was skipped, was cancelled, or was not triggered for approximately 12.35 hours prior to the eval run at 2026-09-30T01:06:31Z. This is an eval-detected workflow staleness condition; no evidence of a user-facing website outage is present in the supplied packet.

failed-check.evidence: overall='major_outage' — the snapshot itself reports a major_outage status, which is consistent with a workflow that last ran during an outage period and has not been refreshed since.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses, confirming the public website and the /observability page are reachable; the failure is isolated to the freshness of the snapshot JSON, not the serving layer.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload, confirming the age value is read directly from the live published artifact.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that regenerates and publishes the observability snapshot failed, was cancelled, or was not triggered for ~12+ hours, leaving the previously published snapshot in place and growing stale.

Second: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deploy or artifact upload) failed silently, so the snapshot file at the published URL was not updated even though the workflow appeared to complete.
Third: A GitHub Actions quota, runner availability, or repository permissions issue prevented the workflow from executing during the expected window.
Fourth: The workflow was manually disabled, paused, or had its schedule removed or altered, causing it to stop running on its normal cadence.

Fifth (lower confidence): A CDN or GitHub Pages caching layer is serving a stale version of status.json despite a successful workflow publish — this would be disproved if the workflow run history shows a recent successful run.
